assumptions: The slowness was attributed to the new code path itself rather than to a downstream service that only that path calls. The retrieved logs name no upstream call or timeout, so the dependency explanation was neither confirmed nor ruled out - it was set aside as unsupported by evidence, not disproven. The p99-only latency shape is consistent with either.

Causation from the flag was inferred from timing and from the absence of any other change (no deploys or config changes in the prior 24 hours, flat traffic and memory), not from tracing or profiling of the monthly-spend path.

Recovery was inferred from metrics returning to baseline after the flag revert. Because the elevated latency lasted only a few minutes, it is assumed the revert caused the recovery rather than the condition clearing on its own.

The small rise in failed requests is assumed to be a consequence of the slow page - shoppers abandoning loads, which the service logs as ClientDisconnected. Note that the same ClientDisconnected errors appear at comparable rates for the half hour before onset, so the flag is not clearly the source of all of them.
The first minute of the window (14:46) was only partially rolled out, so not all shoppers in that minute were exposed to the slow path.

The change-event lookup over the 24 hours before onset returned nothing; only a narrower 15-minute query surfaced the flag change. Completeness of the change record outside those windows was not verified.
The proposed draft pull request has not been reviewed, tested, or shown to fix the underlying slowness.
input.executive_summary:
On 21 September 2026, shoppers loading the account page on the online store saw it respond very slowly - the slowest requests went from roughly a fifth of a second to close to two seconds. The problem began at 14:46 UTC and the page was back to its normal speed by 14:52 UTC, a window of about six minutes. Only the account page was affected; the store stayed up, traffic was normal throughout, and the great majority of requests still succeeded, with only a slight increase in the share that failed over the baseline rate the page already ran at.

The cause was a newly switched-on monthly spending summary on the account page, which was turned on for all shoppers within a minute or two of the ramp starting. The new summary is slow to produce. The automated responder picked up the alert, traced the slowdown to that one change, switched the feature back off, and then watched the page until it confirmed the speed had returned to normal. Total time from alert to confirmed fix was about a minute. A draft code change to address the slow summary has been opened for the owning team to review; the feature remains off until then.
input.root_cause: The `monthly-spend-feature` flag was switched from off to on, beginning a ramp at 14:46 (145 off / 55 on) and reaching 100% of evaluations by 14:47; the new monthly-spend code path on the account page is slow, and p99 latency went from its ~200ms baseline to 1891ms in the first fully-rolled-out minute and stayed roughly in the 950-1900ms band until the flag was reverted. Nothing else about the service changed in that window - no deploy or config change in the preceding 24 hours, request rate steady at ~1200 rpm, memory flat - and p50/p95 stayed flat while only p99 spiked, which is the shape of a slow path taken by a subset of requests.
